_note: Data for the parent guide kit/after-a-paddling.md (built by tools/lib/after-a-paddling.mjs). Every statute and deadline was read on 2026-10-29 at the state's own statute site unless the text says otherwise (Mississippi: Justia; Tennessee: read in the official LexisNexis-hosted code's search view). Lawyer resources read on each organization's own page the same day; protection and advocacy designations checked against the NDRN member directory. Plain-language summaries of statute text; the fact files in facts/claims/ carry the verbatim quotes. Each entry: consent_rule, immunity_quote (verbatim), immunity_cite, immunity_url, notice_of_claim, limitation, minor_tolling (+ cites and urls), bar_referral, protection_advocacy, legal_aid, sea_complaint, law_school_clinics.

AL.notice_of_claim: No statute names a school board. The six-month tort claim rule is for municipalities only. Alabama's constitution says the State may never be made a defendant in any court (Art. I, § 14); ask a lawyer whether a board of education shares that immunity.
AL.limitation: Two years for any injury to the person.
AL.minor_tolling: Yes. A child under nineteen has until two years after turning nineteen.

bar_referral.name: Alabama State Bar Lawyer Referral Service

sea_complaint.name: Alabama State Department of Education, special education dispute resolution

law_school_clinics.name: Children's Rights Clinic, University of Alabama School of Law

AL.consent_rule: None in the statute; the local board's policy decides.
AL.immunity_quote: So long as teachers follow approved policy in the exercise of their responsibility to maintain discipline in their classroom, such teacher shall be immune from civil or criminal liability.

AR.notice_of_claim: None in the immunity statute. School districts are immune from suit for damages except to the extent they carry liability insurance, and no tort action lies against the district for its employees' acts; the claim is against the insurance.
AR.limitation: Three years is the period in § 16-56-105; the specific item covering injury to the person could not be read on the official site, so confirm it with a lawyer.
AR.minor_tolling: Yes. A person under twenty-one when the claim accrues may sue within three years after reaching full age.

bar_referral.name: Arkansas Bar Association Find a Lawyer directory (no referral service)

sea_complaint.name: Arkansas Division of Elementary and Secondary Education, state complaints

AR.consent_rule: None in the statute; the district's written discipline policy must authorize it.
AR.immunity_quote: teachers and administrators in a school district that authorizes use of corporal punishment in the school district's written student discipline policy shall be immune from any civil liability for administering corporal punishment to students, provided only that the corporal punishment is administered in substantial compliance with the school district's written student discipline policy. [...] A teacher or administrator [...] is not immune from civil liability under subdivision (a)(1) of this section if the teacher or administrator uses corporal punishment on a child who is intellectually disabled, nonambulatory, nonverbal, or autistic.

AZ.notice_of_claim: Yes. A written claim stating the facts and a settlement amount must be filed with the district within one hundred eighty days of when you knew of the injury, or it is barred. The claim is deemed denied after sixty days.
AZ.limitation: One year for any action against a public entity or employee; two years for personal injury generally.
AZ.minor_tolling: Partly. A minor may file the claim within one hundred eighty days after turning eighteen; the general tolling rule is separate.

bar_referral.name: Maricopa County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (the State Bar runs none)

law_school_clinics.name: Education Advocacy Clinic, University of Arizona James E. Rogers College of Law

AZ.consent_rule: None in the statute; the board sets the procedures.
AZ.immunity_none: No immunity clause: the words immune and liable do not appear in the school discipline statute.

FL.notice_of_claim: Yes. A written claim to the agency and to the Department of Financial Services within three years, and a denial, before suit. The statute does not name school boards; a lawyer must confirm how it applies to a district.
FL.limitation: Four years for a claim under the sovereign immunity statute; generally two years for negligence and four for battery.
FL.minor_tolling: Rarely. Minority pauses the clock only while the child has no parent or guardian able to sue, and never beyond seven years. Nothing in § 768.28 pauses the claim deadline.

bar_referral.name: The Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service

sea_complaint.name: Florida Department of Education, dispute resolution

law_school_clinics.name: Children & Youth Law Clinic, University of Miami School of Law

FL.consent_rule: Opt-in. A board that allows it must require parental consent, for the year or before each paddling (§ 1002.20(4)(c), since July 1, 2025).
FL.immunity_quote: An officer, employee, or agent of the state or of any of its subdivisions may not be held personally liable in tort or named as a party defendant in any action for any injury or damage suffered as a result of any act, event, or omission of action in the scope of her or his employment or function, unless such officer, employee, or agent acted in bad faith or with malicious purpose or in a manner exhibiting wanton and willful disregard of human rights, safety, or property.
FL.immunity_cite: Fla. Stat. § 768.28(9)(a) (general employee immunity; the school statutes have no corporal punishment immunity clause)

GA.notice_of_claim: None found. The six-month municipal notice and the twelve-month county and state rules do not name school districts, and the state Tort Claims Act excludes them. Separately, a teacher who paddles in good faith under board policy is not liable in a civil or criminal action.
GA.limitation: Two years for injuries to the person.
GA.minor_tolling: Yes. A child has the same two years after turning eighteen.

bar_referral.name: State Bar of Georgia Find a Lawyer (lists local referral services)

sea_complaint.name: Georgia Department of Education, dispute resolution

GA.consent_rule: Opt-out by physician only: a statement from a medical doctor licensed in Georgia, filed on the day of enrollment (§ 20-2-731(5)).
GA.immunity_quote: No principal or teacher who shall administer corporal punishment to a pupil or pupils under his care and supervision in conformity with the policies and regulations of the area, county, or independent board of education employing him and in accordance also with this subpart shall be held accountable or liable in any criminal or civil action based upon the administering of corporal punishment where the corporal punishment is administered in good faith and is not excessive or unduly severe.

IN.notice_of_claim: Yes. Written notice to the school board (and the state political subdivision risk management commission, where it applies) within one hundred eighty days of the loss, or the claim is barred; suit only after denial. A separate pre-suit notice applies to suits against public schools.
IN.limitation: Two years for injury to the person.
IN.minor_tolling: For the suit, yes: two years after the disability ends. For the notice, only an incapacitated person gets one hundred eighty days after the incapacity ends; ask a lawyer whether a child qualifies.

bar_referral.name: Indiana courts: Getting Legal Help (links the State Bar directory)

sea_complaint.name: Indiana Department of Education, dispute resolution

IN.consent_rule: None in the statute, which does not mention corporal punishment.
IN.immunity_quote: have qualified immunity with respect to a disciplinary action taken to promote student conduct under subdivision (2) if the action is taken in good faith and is reasonable.

KS.notice_of_claim: Yes. Written notice to the clerk or the school board before any suit; no suit until the claim is denied or one hundred twenty days pass. The notice has no deadline of its own, but the suit must still meet the limitation period, with at least ninety days after denial.
KS.minor_tolling: Yes for the suit: a child may sue within one year after turning eighteen, but never more than eight years after the act. The notice statute says nothing about minors.

bar_referral.name: Kansas Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service

sea_complaint.name: Kansas State Department of Education, dispute resolution

KS.consent_rule: None. Kansas has no school corporal punishment statute.
KS.immunity_none: No school statute and no immunity clause. The only statute on the subject is the criminal child abuse law, which punishes knowingly inflicting cruel and inhuman corporal punishment.

KY.notice_of_claim: None for a local school board. The Board of Claims rules apply only to the Commonwealth and its agencies.
KY.limitation: One year for injury to the person.
KY.minor_tolling: Yes. A child has the same one year after the disability is removed.

bar_referral.name: Kentucky Bar Association: local lawyer referral services

sea_complaint.name: Kentucky Department of Education, dispute resolution

KY.consent_rule: Opt-in by regulation: annual written consent plus verbal consent before each instance (704 KAR 7:170 § 3). Every district has prohibited it.
KY.immunity_none: No civil immunity clause. The criminal code makes a teacher's force justifiable when the teacher believes it necessary to maintain reasonable discipline in a school, class, or other group and it is not designed to cause serious injury.

LA.notice_of_claim: None. The Governmental Claims Act requires no pre-suit notice, and a school board is a political subdivision under it. Suit must be in a Louisiana state court, and damages for one person are capped at five hundred thousand dollars.
LA.limitation: Two years for injuries on or after July 1, 2024; one year for earlier injuries.
LA.minor_tolling: No. Prescription runs against minors. The suspension between parents and children during minority concerns a child's claims against the parents, not a school.

bar_referral.name: Louisiana State Bar Association: Find Legal Help

sea_complaint.name: Louisiana Department of Education, dispute resolution

law_school_clinics.name: Loyola University New Orleans College of Law

LA.consent_rule: Opt-in: written consent each school year on the state Department of Education form (R.S. 17:416.1(B)(1)).
LA.immunity_quote: Should any teacher, principal, or administrator in the public school system be sued for damages by any student, the parent of any student or other persons qualified to bring suit on behalf of such student based upon the act or omission of such teacher, principal, or administrator in the directing of and disciplining of school children under their care and supervision, it shall be the responsibility of the school board employing such teacher, principal, or administrator to provide such defendant with a legal defense to such suit including reasonable attorney fees, investigatory costs, and other related expenses. Should any such teacher, principal, or administrator be cast in judgment for damages in such suit, it shall be the obligation of the school board employing such defendant to indemnify him fully against such judgment [...]

MO.notice_of_claim: None for school districts. Sovereign immunity is waived only for motor vehicles and dangerous property conditions, and only to the extent of insurance.
MO.limitation: Two years for assault and battery; five years for other injury to the person.
MO.minor_tolling: Yes. A person under twenty-one when the claim accrues has the full period after the disability is removed.

legal_aid.name: Legal Services of Missouri (four regional programs)

sea_complaint.name: Missouri DESE, child complaint and due process

MO.consent_rule: Opt-in: the parent is notified and gives written permission (RSMo 160.261.1).
MO.immunity_quote: Spanking, when administered by certificated personnel and in the presence of a witness who is an employee of the school district, or the use of reasonable force to protect persons or property, when administered by personnel of a school district in a reasonable manner in accordance with the local board of education's written policy of discipline, is not abuse within the meaning of chapter 210.
MO.immunity_cite: RSMo 160.261.10; see also 160.261.8 (no civil liability when acting in conformity with board policy)

MS.notice_of_claim: Yes. A notice of claim to the district's chief executive officer at least ninety days before suit; suit within one year of the incident, with the notice pausing the clock ninety-five days. Missing the window is an absolute bar. Read at Justia; the state's official code site could not be opened.
MS.limitation: One year under the Tort Claims Act; three years generally.
MS.minor_tolling: Yes. A child may bring the action within the time allowed after the disability is removed. The statute does not say whether the ninety-day notice is also deferred.

bar_referral.name: The Mississippi Bar Find a Lawyer directory (the Bar runs no referral service)

sea_complaint.name: Mississippi Department of Education, dispute resolution

MS.immunity_quote: No public school teacher, assistant teacher, principal or assistant principal so acting shall be held liable in a suit for civil damages alleged to have been suffered by a student as a result of the administration of corporal punishment, or the taking of action to maintain control and discipline of a student, unless the court determines that the teacher, assistant teacher, principal or assistant principal acted in bad faith or with malicious purpose or in a manner exhibiting a wanton and willful disregard of human rights or safety. [...] No school personnel shall be granted immunity from liability under subsection (2) of this section for the use of corporal punishment on a student with a disability.

NC.notice_of_claim: None for ordinary tort claims against a local board; the Industrial Commission route covers school bus claims only. The board's immunity is waived only to the extent of its liability insurance.
NC.minor_tolling: Yes. A child has the full three years after turning eighteen.

bar_referral.name: North Carolina Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service

sea_complaint.name: NC Department of Public Instruction, dispute resolution

law_school_clinics.name: Children's Law Clinic, Duke University School of Law

NC.consent_rule: Opt-out: a written statement on a form offered at enrollment (G.S. 115C-390.4(b)(6)). Every district has prohibited it.
NC.immunity_none: No immunity clause. The statute defines excessive force as force that results in injury to the child that requires medical attention beyond simple first aid, and a separate statute lets a judge award the teacher's attorney fee against a frivolous suit (G.S. 6-21.4).

OK.notice_of_claim: Yes. A written claim filed with the clerk of the school board within one year of the loss, or it is forever barred; suit within one hundred eighty days after the claim is denied, or deemed denied at ninety days. The Act also exempts the use of necessary and reasonable force by a school employee to control and discipline a student.
OK.limitation: Under the Governmental Tort Claims Act, the one-year claim and then one hundred eighty days. Generally two years for injury, one year for assault and battery.
OK.minor_tolling: Not for the claim. The Act pauses the notice deadline only for up to ninety days of incapacity from the injury. The general rule giving a child one year after the disability ends does not mention the Act.

bar_referral.name: Oklahoma Bar Association Find a Lawyer directory

sea_complaint.name: Oklahoma State Department of Education, dispute resolution

OK.immunity_none: No immunity clause in the school statutes. The child abuse act does not prohibit ordinary force as a means of discipline, including but not limited to spanking, switching or paddling (21 O.S. § 844), and the Governmental Tort Claims Act exempts the use of necessary and reasonable force by a school district employee to control and discipline a student (51 O.S. § 155(35)).

SC.notice_of_claim: Optional. A verified claim may be filed with the district within one year; it is not required, but filing it extends the time to sue from two years to three.
SC.limitation: Two years under the Tort Claims Act, three if a verified claim was filed; three years generally.
SC.minor_tolling: Yes, and the statute names the Tort Claims Act. The years under eighteen do not count, but the suit must be filed within one year after the child turns eighteen.

bar_referral.name: South Carolina Bar Lawyer Referral Service

sea_complaint.name: SC Department of Education, dispute resolution

law_school_clinics.name: Education Rights Clinic, University of South Carolina Joseph F. Rice School of Law

SC.immunity_none: No immunity clause; the statute is one sentence. The Tort Claims Act bars liability for the supervision or control of a student except when the responsibility or duty is exercised in a grossly negligent manner (§ 15-78-60(25)).

TN.notice_of_claim: None. The Governmental Tort Liability Act's former procedural notice section (§ 29-20-302) is repealed. If a claim is denied, suit is in circuit court, only where the Act removes immunity.
TN.limitation: Twelve months under the Governmental Tort Liability Act; one year for injuries to the person generally, two years if criminal charges are brought over the injury.
TN.minor_tolling: Yes for the general limitation period: a person under eighteen may sue after legal rights are restored, within the limitation period, up to three years. The statute does not say whether this reaches the Act's twelve-month period; ask a lawyer.

bar_referral.name: Tennessee Bar Association Find an Attorney (lists city bar referral services)

sea_complaint.name: Tennessee Department of Education, dispute resolution

law_school_clinics.name: Youth Opportunity Clinic, Vanderbilt Law School

TN.consent_rule: None for most students. For a student with a disability, prohibited unless district policy allows it and the parent gives written permission stating the type and circumstances (§ 49-6-4103(b)).
TN.immunity_none: No immunity clause in the corporal punishment sections. Before any paddling the teacher or principal must document in the student's record that they addressed the behavior, gave consequences, consulted the parent and considered a disability evaluation (§ 49-6-4103(a)(2)).

TX.notice_of_claim: Yes. The district is entitled to written notice within six months of the incident, describing the injury, the time and place, and the incident; not required if the district has actual notice of the injury. To sue a professional employee personally: written notice ninety days before suit and exhaustion of the district's grievance process. The Tort Claims Act does not reach school districts except for motor vehicles, or any intentional tort, including disciplinary action by school authorities.
TX.minor_tolling: Yes for the suit: time under eighteen is not counted. The six-month notice statute says nothing about minors.

bar_referral.name: State Bar of Texas Lawyer Referral and Information Service

law_school_clinics.name: Children's Rights Clinic, The University of Texas at Austin School of Law

TX.consent_rule: Opt-out: a signed written statement to the board each school year (§ 37.0011(c)).
TX.immunity_quote: A professional employee of a school district may not be subject to disciplinary proceedings for the employee's use of physical force against a student to the extent justified under Section 9.62, Penal Code. [...] This section does not prohibit a school district from: (1) enforcing a policy relating to corporal punishment; or (2) [...] bringing a disciplinary proceeding against a professional employee of the district who violates the district policy relating to corporal punishment.
TX.immunity_cite: Tex. Educ. Code § 22.0512; Penal Code § 9.62 (force is justified when the educator reasonably believes it necessary to maintain discipline in a group)

WY.notice_of_claim: Yes. An itemized written claim, signed under oath, filed at the district's business office within two years of the act; suit within one year after the claim is filed. Governmental entities and employees are immune from any tort except the listed waivers.
WY.limitation: One year after the claim is filed. Generally four years for injury to rights and one year for assault or battery.
WY.minor_tolling: Only for the youngest. A child seven or younger has until the eighth birthday or two years after the act, whichever is longer. The general rule giving a minor three years after the disability ends does not mention the Act.

bar_referral.name: Wyoming State Bar Lawyer Referral Service and Modest Means Program

sea_complaint.name: Wyoming Department of Education, dispute resolution

WY.immunity_quote: Teachers, principals and superintendents in each district shall be immune from civil and criminal liability in the exercise of reasonable corporal discipline of a student as authorized by board policy.
